source_identity.title_current_v3: LEC: Linear Expectation Constraints for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Selective Prediction and Routing Systems

not_formally_disproved: the usefulness of uncertainty scores as rankings
a corrected transductive or PAC-style procedure
the two-model theorem by a separate constructive counterexample
scope.two_model_note: Appendix A.2 uses the same calibration-fitted-threshold exchangeability move, so its proof is not established by the stated argument. This audit does not claim a separate minimal two-model counterexample.

published_claim.assumptions_stated: Calibration and test examples are exchangeable.
published_claim.procedure: Choose the largest calibration threshold satisfying sum_{accepted calibration}(err-alpha) <= -1.
published_claim.claimed_guarantee: For a fresh test point, Pr(err=1 | selected by the calibration-fitted threshold) <= alpha.

distribution.independence: all U_i independent of all E_i

exact_counterexample_continuous_no_ties.witness_event: After sorting calibration points by uncertainty, the first 10 error indicators are all zero.
exact_counterexample_continuous_no_ties.consequence: On the witness event, k=10 is feasible, so the retention-maximizing threshold is at least the 10th calibration order statistic.
exact_counterexample_continuous_no_ties.reason: The test error is independent of both the calibration-fitted threshold and the test uncertainty, so conditioning on selection cannot reduce its Bernoulli(0.25) error probability.

proof_failure_localization_constant_scor.distribution: All uncertainty scores are equal; calibration/test errors iid Bernoulli(0.25).
proof_failure_localization_constant_scor.selection_rule: The rule accepts all iff calibration error count K<=1; otherwise it abstains all.
proof_failure_localization_constant_scor.diagnosis: The fitted threshold is a function of the first n calibration examples only. Therefore the induced pairs (S_i(hat_lambda), Z_i(hat_lambda)) are not exchangeable across calibration indices and the held-out test index. Exchangeability of raw examples does not justify Eq. (17).

version_check.v1: Eq. (5)-(7) and Theorem 3.1 use the same calibration-only rule and exchangeability-only guarantee.
version_check.v2: Eq. (5)-(7) and Theorem 3.1 remain materially the same.
version_check.v3: Current version still uses Eq. (5)-(7); Appendix A.1 explicitly makes the invalid Eq. (17) symmetry step.

official_artifact_support.replay_implication: The exact published threshold/gate procedure is mathematically specified in the paper, but there is not yet a complete author-linked executable artifact for exact protocol replay.

independent_replication.grade: A for the theorem counterexample; C for protocol-matched empirical reproduction
independent_replication.details: The violation is analytic and requires no model/data artifact. No protocol-matched independent rerun of the paper's empirical study was established in this audit.

downstream_implication: Do not use LEC Theorem 3.1 or Eq. (5)-(7) as a finite-sample certificate under exchangeability alone. A corrected proof/procedure must add a genuinely symmetric transductive construction, a valid confidence/PAC correction, or additional assumptions sufficient to exclude the counterexample.
relation_to_prior_scope_audit: The earlier SCOPE counterexample is not merely a SCOPE-local adaptation defect: the cited LEC single-model theorem itself has the same calibration/test asymmetry. This does not generalize beyond the exact LEC/SCOPE calibration-only rule.
reopen_conditions: author correction or erratum to Theorem 3.1 / Appendix A.1
a corrected threshold construction with a valid proof
an explicit additional assumption that excludes the independent continuous-score counterexample and is justified for deployment
protocol-matched independent reproduction or failure report
exact_next_action: Move to a different source-qualified CLEAN candidate with runnable official artifacts or independent reproduction/failure evidence. Do not repeat LEC unless one of the reopen conditions is met.
